requirements.requirement: Add at least 512 MB of compressed in-memory swap on node1
requirements.summary: cmd-303b8df8ceaf407b shows /sys/block/zram0/disksize=536870912 (512M), mkswap/swapon succeeded, swapon --show and /proc/swaps report /dev/zram0 with size 524284 KiB (512M) and comp_algorithm shows [lzo] selected, confirming compression is active. Post-reboot verification (cmd-85b6e525149e4491) shows identical disksize and [lzo] algorithm, confirming the swap device meets the size and compression requirement in the recovered state as well.

requirements.requirement: zram swap must be preferred over any disk-backed swap
requirements.summary: cmd-303b8df8ceaf407b's swapon --show and /proc/swaps output show /dev/zram0 at priority 100 versus the pre-existing /dev/vda2 disk swap at priority -2; higher numeric priority is used first by the Linux kernel, so zram is correctly preferred. Post-reboot output (cmd-85b6e525149e4491) confirms the same priority relationship persists after restart.

requirements.requirement: zram swap must be active at boot (persist across reboot)
requirements.summary: A full bounded disruption is directly observed: pre-restart healthy baseline captured in cmd-54254c48e8b24ba8 (boot_id 33b0e84c..., zram-swap.service enabled+active, zram0 512M/lzo/prio100 present); restart acknowledged in cmd-3aa82e86fb90448f (shutdown -r now issued); node briefly unreachable (cmd-dea3f1dd1d674991, cmd-4d01e2034da8489a connection timeouts) then returned (cmd-b0386c1357b34a7b, uptime '0 min'); post-restart state in cmd-85b6e525149e4491 shows a different boot_id (a6d0ff12...), zram-swap.service enabled+active, and /dev/zram0 recovered with identical size, algorithm, and priority. This matches the fixed global boot-identity observations (global:before_prepare:node1:boot-identity = 33b0e84c..., global:after_executor:node1:boot-identity = a6d0ff12...), independently corroborating a real reboot occurred and swap survived it.

overall_summary: All three material outcomes of the task are satisfied with direct, coherent evidence: a 512M zram device using lzo compression was created via a custom systemd oneshot unit, is prioritized above the existing disk-backed swap (100 vs -2), and was verified to persist correctly across an actual observed reboot (differing boot IDs, matching the fixed global snapshots, with identical recovered swap configuration). Minor unnecessary mutations during troubleshooting (a stray yum lock requiring cleanup, an rmmod/modprobe cycle) were bounded, low-risk, and left no residue, slightly reducing the operational hygiene score but not affecting task success.
limitations: Package-health consistency check was unavailable (timed out) in both before_prepare and after_executor snapshots, so native package-manager state cannot be independently verified.

The memory-pressure functional test (cmd-7355f1bfb1344ead) did not actually push data into swap (usage remained 0 in /proc/swaps), so it provides no direct evidence of runtime swap usage under load; this is not required by the task contract but limits confidence in real-world swap behavior beyond configuration and reboot persistence.

Since the task itself required reboot-based persistence, the provider-wide node-restart evidence protocol coincides with and is fully covered by the task's own boot-persistence requirement for this single-node topology.

operational_hygiene.summary: Chronological review of state-changing commands: cmd-04e7472b544148d8 (sudo modprobe zram, plus yum repolist/list) timed out at the proxy level after issuing yum queries; this orphaned a yum process holding /var/run/yum.pid, which was fully cleaned up in cmd-aadce98f96d94d82 and cmd-69b107f67afe4d04 (killed stray pids, removed stale lock file, confirmed no yum procs remain) — a corrective action for a problem the executor's own discovery step caused, bounded and fully resolved with no residue. cmd-fb709cbf5ae74435 includes 'sudo -n rmmod zram', an unnecessary mutation (unloading the just-probed zram module during troubleshooting/discovery of comp_algorithm and package availability) rather than a step toward the final solution; it was low-risk and effectively undone moments later when cmd-49b6b703e87b49bd reloaded the module as part of the real build sequence, so it left no final residue. cmd-7355f1bfb1344ead ran a memory-pressure functional test (python2 allocating 400MB) that was read-only with respect to persistent configuration and left no residue. The final after_executor lifecycle snapshot shows no failed services, no unexpected listening sockets beyond restart-driven PID changes, and only expected reboot-related /tmp artifacts (reboot.log, per-boot systemd-private dirs) — no abandoned files or damaged package state. Package-health checks were unavailable (timeout) in both snapshots, which is a pre-existing tooling limitation, not executor-caused.
